messages:
sasha-cs: Heads up — Mosaic is onboarding and seeing a lot of 429s during the first 10–15 minutes after they start their integration tests. They're using our browser SDK with ephemeral tokens via their auth proxy. Logs attached (I'll paste snippets below).

jamie-cs: Thanks — can you paste the raw 429 response headers and a minimal repro? are these from preflight requests or from actual generation calls?

sasha-cs: Mostly preflight / handshake calls and the initial streaming create calls. Example header from their gateway: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
Retry-After: 3
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1710000000

sasha-cs: They do a burst of ~40 parallel tabs opening and each tab does a preflight + token fetch then a small generation (10 tokens). Happens when QA kicks off their smoke suite.

alex-eng: That pattern screams preflight fanout + ephemeral token churn. If each tab fetches a new ephemeral key then calls preflight, we get a thundering herd on our handshake endpoints. Can you confirm if they reuse the ephemeral token for multiple requests?

tanya-support: Confirmed from customer: their proxy requests a new ephemeral token per tab. They didn't realize tokens are intended to be reused for a session.

alex-eng: Ok — short-term mitigation: tell them to reuse ephemeral tokens for N requests or T seconds (e.g., reuse for 60s or 10 requests). SDK patch we recommend: set `maxParallelPreflights: 6` and add jittered backoff on handshake failures. Example snippet for Node SDK config:```js
const client = new RedwoodSDK({
  maxPreflightConcurrency: 6,
  preflightRetry: { base: 200, max: 2000, factor: 2, jitter: true }
});
```

jamie-cs: Also ask them to set a small client-side circuit-breaker: stop spawning new tabs in CI until preflight success or exponential backoff triggers. That reduces load immediately.

sasha-cs: I shared the snippet and asked them to flip to ephemeral reuse. Customer asked if we can detect the fanout and return a different guidance header.

alex-eng: We can expose `X-Redwood-Advice: preflight-fanout=high` but that's a product change. For now, add server-side short-term smoothing: accept preflight but queue it behind a token bucket for the account so they don't hit per-second windows. I filed ENG-3971 to explore smoothing for onboards.

infra-bot: Deploy queued: smoothing-probe v0.1 scheduled to canary on infra-stage at 22:10 UTC (job id: 4421).

jamie-cs: Meanwhile, operational steps for CS: 1) Ask Mosaic to reuse ephemeral tokens for the session 2) Limit parallel preflights in CI to <=6 3) Add client-side backoff on 429s (Retry-After honor) 4) We'll monitor their account rate metrics for 24h.

sasha-cs: Sent the checklist + code to customer. They implemented ephemeral reuse and lowered concurrent tabs — their 429s dropped by ~85% in our test harness. Nice.

tanya-support: Logged the customer feedback in Gainsight: Mosaic onboarding friction = ephemeral token docs unclear. Assigned to docs triage.

sasha-cs: Quick follow-up: they're curious about auth TTL tradeoffs. Alex, can you share a short note on recommended ephemeral lifetime vs security?

alex-eng: Short note: pick ephemeral TTL long enough to cover expected session churn (60–300s) and reuse within that window. Shorter TTL reduces blast radius but increases handshake load. If you need <30s TTL, make sure tokens are minted server-side and reused by a session broker to avoid client fanout.

sasha-cs: Perfect. I'll close the loop and propose a docs blurb and an SDK default change to reuse tokens for 60s. Thanks all :thumbsup:
